correctness.rationale: The conjugacy uses a=kb₁ and domain [−k,k]. On J₀ the four iterates run through k(u−1), u−t, ku+1, u, with the half-open images exactly as claimed, so all four phases are distinct, including the orbit of zero. Off P the three endpoint exceptions are k→t→−1→0. Every orbit that avoids P forever therefore alternates on (t,1) and (−1,−t); the affine return on the positive strip has fixed point p with multiplier k² and no other orbit staying bounded there for all future returns. It follows that the only avoiding points are ±p and every other point outside P is transient. The open strips have total length 2/k, and each inverse step from either entire target strip fits into the opposite strip and divides length by k. The finitely many endpoint preimages at any fixed n have length zero, so the survivor length is 2/k^(n+1). Dividing by domain length 2k and summing the resulting tail gives the exact probability and mean. For the invariant law, write Q=P∪{−p,p}; Q is Borel and forward invariant, and the increasing preimages g⁻ⁿ(Q) exhaust the domain. Invariance and continuity from below give μ(Q)=1, including any potentially atomic measure on an exceptional endpoint. Equal masses on the two-cycle and pushforward of the restriction on J₀ to the other three phases give the displayed unique mixture (with ρ immaterial at α=1). Ergodicity reduces to a point mass on the Borel selector, or to the two-cycle measure.
residual_risks: The phrase 'normalized Lebesgue measure' is read in the sense fixed in the assumptions: the 2/k^(n+1) formula is ordinary length in u, not the probability. The frozen proof's assertion that a transient point always has a neighborhood inside the complement is too strong at −1, t or k; the preimage argument proves the invariant-measure conclusion without that assertion. Frozen rational tests are finite corroboration, not proof of the quantified result.
